record.original_question: Determine the Frobenius variety generated by the symmetric numerical semigroups.

evidence.quote: What is the Frobenius variety generated only by the symmetric ones?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A numerical semigroup is a subset $S \subseteq \mathbb{N} = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$ that is closed under addition, contains $0$, and has finite complement $\mathbb{N}\setminus S$ in $\mathbb{N}$. The Frobenius number $F(S)$ of a numerical semigroup $S \neq \mathbb{N}$ is the largest integer not belonging to $S$. The genus $g(S)$ is the cardinality of $\mathbb{N}\setminus S$. A numerical semigroup $S$ is called symmetric if $g(S) = (F(S)+1)/2$ (equivalently, for every integer $z$, exactly one of $z$ and $F(S)-z$ lies in $S$).

A nonempty family $\mathcal{V}$ of numerical semigroups is called a Frobenius variety if it satisfies:
(i) if $S, T \in \mathcal{V}$, then $S \cap T \in \mathcal{V}$;
(ii) if $S \in \mathcal{V}$ and $S \neq \mathbb{N}$, then $S \cup \{F(S)\} \in \mathcal{V}$.

The intersection of an arbitrary family of Frobenius varieties is again a Frobenius variety, so for any family $\mathcal{F}$ of numerical semigroups there is a unique smallest Frobenius variety containing $\mathcal{F}$, called the Frobenius variety generated by $\mathcal{F}$.

Problem: Give an explicit description (a complete characterization of its members) of the Frobenius variety generated by the family of all symmetric numerical semigroups.
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears in a published problem list on numerical semigroups and is referenced in subsequent literature on Frobenius varieties (e.g., works on Frobenius restricted varieties and covarieties), without an explicit characterization being provided. No source found that claims a full description of the Frobenius variety generated by the symmetric numerical semigroups, so it appears to remain open.
